purpose: This medication is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is used along with diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range. It is not used for type 1 diabetes.
how_it_works: This pill combines two medicines that work in different ways. Empagliflozin works by telling your kidneys to remove extra sugar from your blood through your urine, so your body gets rid of it naturally. Metformin works by reducing the amount of sugar your liver releases into your blood and helping your body use insulin more effectively.
common_side_effects: You may notice more frequent urination since the medication helps flush sugar out through urine. Some people experience nausea, upset stomach, or diarrhea, especially when first starting the medication — taking it with food usually helps. Yeast infections or urinary tract infections can also occur because more sugar passes through the urinary tract.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you notice signs of a urinary tract infection such as burning when you urinate, or signs of a vaginal yeast infection. A rare but serious condition called diabetic ketoacidosis can occur — seek care immediately if you feel very nauseous, have stomach pain, or trouble breathing. This medication should be temporarily stopped before surgeries or certain imaging tests that use contrast dye. Do not take it if you have severe kidney problems.
typical_dosing: This medication is usually taken twice daily with meals to reduce stomach upset. Your doctor will start you on a lower dose and may gradually increase it based on how your blood sugar responds and how well you tolerate it. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and never skip doses without talking to them first.
